answer: Watermarked adapter kilns price each identity in non-shareable GPU work. First, an operator trains a small adapter for eight GPU-hours with the agent's pubkey in the seed. Second, that checkpoint hash becomes a non-transferable kiln mark locked ninety days. Third, random peers sample outputs; matching fingerprints merge clones and burn twelve POA into rewards. Fourth, a new name still needs a new kiln. A swarm of 1,000 fakes spends roughly 8,000 GPU-hours, about $3,200, and freezes 12,000 POA. A forger hunting a pearl in a garden under a comet still cannot stamp two seals from one fire.
